overall: A dry, unhurried voice from someone who has stood near a rig and respects what the work costs, plain about the facts and never selling the robots. The read opens with a small lifted image, settles into steady explanation, drops to its quietest at the injury figure and the company expectations, and lands lower and more certain than its middle.

lines.text: In Midland, a column of drill pipe over two stories tall swings toward the hole. The floorhand pulls back both gloves, because a robot arm already has it.
lines.intent: Open on one concrete image, then turn it with the glove detail.
lines.note: Weight on swings, then a small dry turn on already. Midland is said the local way, not announced.

lines.text: On this ExxonMobil rig, robotic arms set the pipe in place and connect it to the drill string. Crews on the floor used to help do that by hand.
lines.intent: Explain what changed in plain terms.
lines.note: Even and matter of fact. Emphasis on by hand, as a quiet contrast with the arms.

lines.text: So the floor gets a fence. The gate carries a sign that reads Red Zone, with a drawing of the Grim Reaper.
lines.intent: A wry detail that shows how seriously the site takes the danger.
lines.note: A half smile on the Grim Reaper, underplayed. The sign is read as a fact, not a joke.

lines.text: Exxon's Bart Cahir says about a third of significant drilling injuries have happened right here, on the rig floor.
lines.intent: Land the reason for the fence with the key safety fact.
lines.note: Quietest delivery so far. The fraction is said flat with no lift, and weight falls on right here.

lines.text: Drilling contractor Helmerich and Payne supplies the system. Three arms move pipe weighing roughly 2,000 pounds. One walks each stand to the hole, one lines up the threads, and one racks pipe high in the derrick.
lines.intent: Inventory of the machine, three jobs for three arms.
lines.note: Brisk and even. The three arm jobs run as a list with a light stress on each verb: walks, lines up, racks. Risk: long line, trim supplier detail first if it runs over.

lines.text: So where did the crew go? Up into a small office on the rig, where a contractor runs the robots with controls on a screen.
lines.intent: Turn with a question, then answer it flatly.
lines.note: The question is genuine and a touch curious. The answer comes lower and drier, with weight on small office.

lines.text: That contractor is the driller, who starts each move and watches it, and the arms follow paths planned in advance. The crew works out the exact moves with an Exxon operations team in Houston.
lines.intent: Establish that a person still runs the work and the plan comes from people.
lines.note: Steady and explanatory. Emphasis on starts each move and watches it. Houston is given no extra weight.

lines.text: Exxon runs more than 30 rigs in the Permian, and in August, Reuters counted two that were automated. Exxon plans to automate more than half its unconventional fleet by the end of 2028.
lines.intent: Scale: how few now, how many planned.
lines.note: Two is delivered small and plain, then the plan is said with a measured rise. Emphasis on two.

lines.text: The first one already set a pace. It drilled two miles sideways underground in a little over six days, the third fastest time in Exxon's history.
lines.note: The highest point of the read, still understated. Weight on sideways, then third fastest is stated as a ranking, not a boast.

lines.text: Does a robot take a job? Exxon expects similar staffing, and calls it a force multiplier, not a replacement. It also believes it could prevent roughly a third of high-consequence incidents. Both are company expectations, not counts.
lines.intent: Face the jobs question honestly and mark the claims as the company's own.
lines.note: Drop from the previous line. The question is plain, not rhetorical. The last sentence is the quietest and most careful, with emphasis on expectations.

lines.text: Cahir says people off the floor can plan the next operation instead. So who tightens the pipe now? A robot arm does. A person still decides when.
lines.intent: Close on the answer to the opening image, certain and low.
lines.note: Lands lower and more certain than the middle. A robot arm does is short and flat. The final line is said at conversation pace with weight on decides, no lift at the end.
